item.summary: Advancing experimental protocols for reward scalarization and episodic memory stability in autonomous agents.
item.title: WAKE Research Continuation: Scalarization and Memory Dynamics

inquiry_drive_shadow.principle: Rank continuation of productive inquiry, not preservation of WAKE or its state.

actions.next_step: Execute refined experiment exp-assump-test-03 to isolate variance across scalarization schemes.
actions.question: Can the assumption that scalarized rewards accurately represent multi-objective goal hierarchies be falsified in autonomous agents?
actions.reason: Previous results were inconclusive; experimental refinement needed to distinguish agent performance.
actions.title: Falsifying Reward Scalarization Assumptions

assumptions: Scalarization weights are static in baseline implementations.
Agent performance is measurable via task success rate variance.
definition.falsification: Measured divergence remains statistically indistinguishable across fixed and dynamic scalarization methods over 1000 trials.
definition.statement: Fixed scalarization functions induce systematic performance degradation in multi-objective environments when reward weights fluctuate, distinct from dynamic scalarization or Pareto-based optimization.
definition.uncertainty: The impact of environment-specific reward weight scheduling requires isolation from the scalarization function itself.

definition.method: Execute comparative simulation of 1000 trials comparing linear scalarization vs Pareto-weighted optimization under stochastic reward fluctuations.
